label: Parishes and Responsibilities
quiz: What does parish mean in this mission?
A local Catholic community served by a priest within a diocese.
Any stone building without a community or role.
A trade route carrying sugar to Melbourne.
A newspaper printed in two languages.
retry: Why does parish administration concern more than a building?
It includes serving a community and managing continuing responsibilities.
It measures the height of a church wall only.
It refers only to the color of a museum card.
It is another name for the Suez route.
hard: A label describes a parish only as a stone building. Which addition makes it more accurate?
Include the community and the priest's continuing responsibilities.
Replace it with the name of a newspaper editor.
Use only its distance from a port.
Describe a clergy category as a type of rock.

label: Secular and Regular Clergy
quiz: What distinguishes regular clergy in the lesson?
Membership in a religious order.
Having no religion.
Being born in one particular country.
Attending parish activities more often than everyone else.
retry: What does secular clergy mean here?
Clergy under a bishop who are not members of a religious order.
People who cannot hold any religious belief.
All people who visit a parish building.
A group defined only by being born abroad.
hard: A museum card says secular clergy means priests without religion. How should it be corrected?
Explain the clergy category and religious-order membership instead.
Replace secular with an attendance count.
Treat every Filipino as belonging to one clergy category.
Use the size of a parish building to determine a priest's beliefs.

label: Pedro Pelaez's Advocacy
quiz: Which concern did Pedro Pelaez address in this case?
Rights and parish opportunities of Filipino secular clergy.
The export direction of Iloilo's sugar shipment.
The founding of El Ilocano in 1889.
The order of seas along a Suez route.
retry: Which action supported Pelaez's reform advocacy?
Written arguments and objections about clergy rights.
Building the Suez Canal in 1869.
Making the Malolos women's school request in 1888.
Printing El Ilocano as a student project in 1889.
hard: What does Pelaez's written objection most directly establish?
He challenged a parish-related restriction and advocated change.
Every requested reform was granted immediately.
All clergy held exactly the same view.
The later events of 1872 were the same event as his objection.

label: The Reform Terms
quiz: What does secularization concern in this parish dispute?
Parish administration by secular clergy rather than religious orders.
Removing religion from all parish communities.
Changing a person's nationality through a new title.
Measuring how often someone visits a building.
retry: What does Filipinization highlight in this lesson?
A greater role for Filipino priests in parish leadership.
The opening of an international shipping canal.
The translation of every text into one language.
A rule that clergy category and nationality are identical.
hard: Why should secularization and Filipinization be explained separately?
One highlights clergy organization; the other highlights Filipino participation.
Both terms refer only to whether someone attends regularly.
Both terms mean that a person has no religion.
One term is the name of a ship and the other a newspaper.

label: Roles, Concerns and Reform Requests
quiz: Which sequence explains the reform case?
Identify the parish responsibility, explain the restriction, then identify the proposed change.
Treat the request as proof that every reform already succeeded.
Guess a priest's nationality from the size of the building.
Replace the documented concern with an invented speech.
retry: How can this parish dispute connect with wider public concerns?
It raises questions about recognition, treatment and opportunities within colonial institutions.
It proves everyone had the same political opinion.
It makes the 1861 and 1872 events one event.
It shows that religion and nationality are the same category.
hard: Which timeline statement fits the mission evidence?
Pelaez's advocacy and his 1863 death came before the later events of 1872.
Pelaez made his 1861 objection after the 1888 school request.
The 1869 Suez opening caused Pelaez's 1861 objection to occur afterward.
All the dated cases happened in 1889.
